## Breaking changes

- PostgreSQL >= 13 is required (`xid8`, `pg_current_xact_id()`).
- Run `PostgresStore::Schema.create!` again on existing databases, once per namespace. It adds a `tx_id` column and an index to the events table. Adding the column rewrites the table under an exclusive lock, so run it at a quiet moment on a large log. Until it has run, PostgreSQL appends still work but `subscribe` fails.
- `PostgresStore#subscribe` delivers events in commit order (`tx_id`, then position), not strictly ascending by position. Positions still ascend per tag and within one append. A subscriber waits behind any unfinished write transaction on the server. `after:` still takes a position; resuming from a position taken from `read` rather than from the subscription can redeliver events that committed out of order around it.

## Fixes

- #54: `PostgresStore#subscribe` no longer skips an event whose position was committed after a higher one had been delivered.
- #55: `DecisionModel.build` no longer writes a snapshot past a matching append still in flight (type-only queries, or items on different tags). A snapshot the store cannot vouch for is skipped, and a later build writes it. New store method `settled?(query, after:, through:, count:)`.
- `subscribe` (PostgreSQL and SQLite) starts listening before its catch-up read, so an append committed in between wakes it.
